chapter: Suntaug Lake Inn and Duke Ellington's band
title: How Duke built up a performance after intermission
summary: Hinton and Whaley describe Carney's reliability and Duke calling the band back with 'A Train', 'Mood Indigo' and 'Satin Doll'.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: You know, in observing Duke's band, the guys that always seemed to me most reliable was like Harry Carney, you know, when they took intermission and the band came back out after intermission you could always depend on Carney to be back on time and you could always depend on perhaps in later years, the clarinet player that's down in the West Indies now.

Jimmy Hamilton and I think that's -- I remember once seeing that band, and after intermission Duke would play something, he made this little call -------- he made that little call to call off the men back and the guys were out socializing with the chicks and talking to the customers, Duke would be the only one on the bandstand and pretty soon you see Carney come up and he would start something like Mood Indigo where he only needed three or four of them to get it started.
Can you tell me something about that.
What do you call it, his -- Duke Ellington at the piano and he'd start a number like -------

The "A Train", see, and then go from the A Train he would go into a number for probably Cootie, see, and from then he would give a preparation for 'Mood Indigo' and that's three guys would come out and then he would go into Harry Carney on "Sophisticated Lady" and from Harry he would go into "Satin Doll" and that would close his performance. But he knew how to build up, you know, gradually build it up into man, they are jumping.
Oh, yeah, he had that ability to rise to the occasion and as you say to build it up.
